missionPremise: Three controls that each cannot run or pass on the wrong input, per the dispatch's PLAN-ROW P-334/P-329/P-330 (OPS-16 texas_market_plan_of_record) and OPS-24 Law 2 ('the gate is fixed before anything trusts it'). (1) P-321/P-173 deployed factory-retired-share-watch and it refused TARGET_ENV_MISSING on its FIRST execution (factory-retired-share-watch-m7cv7, 2026-09-18) because its resolver asked for a credential its own deploy case deliberately does not mount -- a control that has never once run. (2) The _LDT_SHA comment-presence control (P-124/CTX-PIN4, hauska-factory #173 / 294bc2c) skipped or crashed on exactly the force-push it exists to see, and accepted a comment anywhere in the file. (3) Since hauska-factory #174, factory-parcel-ag-valuation's DECLARED absences (P-322/A-184: COUNTY_NO_SOURCE_PENDING for 48021, 48055, 48209, 48309; COUNTY_NOT_IN_SCOPE for 48053) stop the county runner at stage 6, so factory-dollar-fields-patch and stages 7-12 never run for those counties through the runner. All three are the same failure shape: a control whose subject cannot reach it.

correctionsToDispatchPremise.dispatchSays: 'P-334's fix ships through cloudbuild.publish.yaml, which rebuilds every publish job from one image (it would also ship P-327's merged gate, and the bake pin is stale until P-351). List exactly which jobs and which merged-but-undeployed changes that rebuild would carry.'
correctionsToDispatchPremise.measured: The rebuild carries THREE merged-but-undeployed rows, not one. The last publish build is Cloud Build e301a363-5a76-4315-adab-75ec6d5f3a68 (create 2026-09-18T10:40:58Z, finish 10:49:21Z, SUCCESS, image tag publish-e301a363-...). Every one of the seven jobs that file deploys runs the same digest, sha256:afbd0bbc914d7b9547751581aac61e2b5a231b88e03c3f93d71e769a0c0ea2a3, read live 2026-09-18 via `gcloud run jobs describe`; the watch job's creationTimestamp is 2026-09-18T10:49:16Z with generation 1, i.e. that build is what created it. Commits merged after that build: #175 P-325 (85d63e8, 10:52:42Z commit), #177 P-327 (807cbad, 15:03:08Z), #178 P-335 (0f4558a, 15:06:37Z) -- all three touch src/, which Dockerfile.publish copies into the image (COPY src ./src; entrypoint `node src/cli.mjs`). So the deployment the seat sequences is: one build, SEVEN jobs redeployed (factory-publish-migrate, factory-staging-reset, factory-bastrop-publish, factory-republish-on-change, factory-verify-walk, factory-dollar-fields-patch, factory-retired-share-watch), carrying P-325 + P-327 + P-335 as well as P-334.
correctionsToDispatchPremise.whyItMatters: The seat merging P-334 alone would still put P-327's retirement gate and P-325/#178's parcel-record-fill changes into the deployed image in the same act, on the same digest, with no separate deploy to point at. Declared here so the sequencing decision is the seat's and is made on the real count.

correctionsToDispatchPremise.dispatchSays: 'The runner learns a child's refusal code from the child's own durable record (its run event or a declared exit code), never by inferring it from a failed execution.'
correctionsToDispatchPremise.measured: There is no 'or'. P-322's own header states the requirement that removes the first channel: parcel-ag-valuation refuses BEFORE any store is opened, so a scope refusal leaves NO runs row and NO run event -- there is no durable record to read. The child's exit status is the ONLY channel that can carry a store-less refusal's code, and Cloud Run keeps it on the task attempt (TaskAttemptResult.exitCode, v2 REST .../executions/{execution}/tasks, read 2026-09-18). The runner therefore reads an exit code (and refuses to infer: an unreadable code, an undeclared code, and a declared-for-another-job code all stop the walk).
correctionsToDispatchPremise.whyItMatters: If the store-less refusal had left a run row, the design would have been 'read the row, verify the code, continue' -- a strictly better control (a row can carry prose). It does not, so the exit code is the contract, which is why the range (60-79) is documented in one module rather than being a per-caller flag.

correctionsToDispatchPremise.dispatchSays: 'the same shape as the depth step's existing `precondition` entry'
correctionsToDispatchPremise.measured: The depth step's `precondition` at 0f4558a was a DECLARATION THE RUNNER ONLY RECORDED, never acted on: county-runner-plan.mjs:267 carried `{code, named, why, ownerRow}` on the STEP, county-runner.mjs:468 wrote it onto the stage record as a note, and a failed child still stopped the run. So the shape to reuse was the declaration's fields, not its effect -- P-330 moves the declaration to the JOB that owns the scope (`scopeRefusals`, one entry per code, with `named` pointing at the file+constant and `ownerRow` kept where it exists), makes the runner act on it, and derives the SAME printed `precondition:` line from the per-job entries so the operator-facing text does not change shape.
correctionsToDispatchPremise.whyItMatters: Stated because 'same shape as the existing entry' could be read as 'the runner already honours it', and it did not -- the note was there while stage 6 stopped.

whatIWillBuild: P-334: `resolveTargetDatabase(env, target)` in src/lib/publish-target-env.mjs -- the database-only resolver, same target discipline (the target's OWN var, no ?? chain, TARGET_UNKNOWN for an unknown target, TARGET_ENV_MISSING naming the missing variable and never its value) and the same `DATABASE_URL` key in the return. publish-retired-share-watch.mjs resolves through it. The secret mount is NOT widened. A new test (test/p334-watch-secret-mount.test.mjs) reads the job's SECRETS list out of cloudbuild.publish.yaml and runs the watch against exactly that environment, so the mount and the resolver cannot disagree silently again -- plus the audit of the one other job with the mirrored shape.

P-329: `resolveBase` in scripts/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs -- the base resolved in ONE place, an unreachable --base falling back to the merge-base with a declared ref (`--fallback-ref`, default origin/main), an unresolvable base refusing with a reason (exit 2) instead of skipping; and adjacency declared once (`PIN_COMMENT_ADJACENCY_LINES = 3`) with the pass requiring an added comment line within that window of the added pin line. The ci.yml job loses its null-sha `if:` and passes the fallback ref, and runs this row's fixture tests too. NOT touched: ldt-pin-staleness, and _LDT_SHA's value never moves in this diff.

P-330: per-job `scopeRefusals` in src/lib/county-runner-plan.mjs (code, the file+constant that owns the scope, why, ownerRow), validated by `validatePlan`; src/lib/scope-refusal-exits.mjs as the ONE place a refusal code becomes an exit status (60-79) and the only reverse lookup; src/cli.mjs exiting with the declared code; src/control/cloudrun-jobs.mjs reading the child's task-attempt exit code and never guessing; src/jobs/county-runner.mjs continuing past a child failure ONLY when the readable code is declared for that job, and recording the step as `refused` with its code.
preRegisteredFalsifiers: P-334/F1 (both directions, ONE script reading the template): `runRetiredShareWatch` with the environment the DEPLOYED job actually holds -- the SECRETS list read from cloudbuild.publish.yaml's factory-retired-share-watch case plus the template's plain env -- must (pre-change) throw TARGET_ENV_MISSING naming PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL and (post-change) read the serving store through the mounted PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL and record one observation. Falsified by: a resolver that still demands the mcp url, or a test that hands it a hand-built full environment (the in-class mistake that hid the defect).

P-334/F2 (the audit, measured not asserted): whether any OTHER job in that template holds the mirrored shape (a resolver wider than its mount). Answer measured: factory-verify-walk mounts FACTORY_DATABASE_URL only while src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs resolves the target PAIR. Asserted as a fact about today's template in the P-334 test file, NOT fixed here.

P-329/F1 (both directions): an unreachable --base (the force-push shape) with --fallback-ref origin/main must (pre-change) exit 2 with `fatal: bad object` and a null-sha push must be SKIPPED by the workflow's `if:` (both silent in effect), and (post-change) resolve to the merge-base, FAIL the branch's own value-only bump (exit 1), and report baseFrom=merge-base. Falsified by: any skip, or any fallback that diffs against a branch TIP (which would read main's newer commits as removals).

P-329/F2 (both directions, at the boundary): a bump whose only added comment sits FOUR lines from the pin must (pre-change) PASS and (post-change) FAIL, and a comment at exactly three lines must PASS, so the constant is measured rather than assumed. Plus: a bare `#` spacer is not a comment (FAIL), and a diff that does not touch the pin VALUE is out of scope (PASS). Falsified by: an adjacency window narrower than the real CTX-PIN shape (0/1), which would get the guard turned off.

P-330/F1 (both directions): ag-valuation refusing COUNTY_NO_SOURCE_PENDING for Hays 48021 must (pre-change) stop stage 6 at that job -- factory-dollar-fields-patch never requested, stage record `failed`/JOB_FAILED, stoppedBecause INSTRUMENT_FAILED, step-6 record outcome=failed -- and (post-change) record the step as `refused` with the code, request factory-dollar-fields-patch, and reach stage 7. Falsified by: a runner that skips the declined job entirely (the declaration is about the ANSWER, not about not asking).

P-330/F2 (the three stopping directions, each its own test): an UNDECLARED code (70, in range but undeclared; and 42, out of range), a failure whose code CANNOT BE READ, and a code declared for a DIFFERENT job must each stop the run. Falsified by: a runner that only asks 'is this code in the table'.

P-330/F3 (the declaration is not a second scope list): every declared code must point at a file that exports a constant WITH THAT VALUE, and validatePlan must refuse a code the CLI cannot emit distinctly, a code declared twice on one job, and a declaration naming no source.
P-329/F3 (the row's own question): whether this change alters what ldt-pin-staleness sees. Must be NO -- checked by reading that workflow and the diff, not by assumption.

P-334.whatExecutesIt: resolveTargetDatabase, called by runRetiredShareWatch (src/jobs/publish-retired-share-watch.mjs) on every execution of the Cloud Run job factory-retired-share-watch, whose template args are `retired-share-watch,--target=production,--apply`.
P-334.whatTriggersIt: Every execution, with no flag to set: the resolver runs before any store is opened. A missing variable refuses before the first connection.
P-334.whatFails: TARGET_ENV_MISSING naming the missing variable (never its value); TARGET_UNKNOWN for a target outside the table. The refused execution exits non-zero and the job's schedule (operator-set, hourly) records a failed execution.
P-334.whatBypassesIt: Setting the variable to a value the store rejects (the resolver checks presence, not reachability); running with --target=<the other target> deliberately; and the deploy case drifting from the resolver in the OTHER direction (a job that mounts MORE than it needs is not caught by this fix -- the test reads the mount and would fail if the mount narrowed further, but a widened mount is merely wasteful).

P-329.whatExecutesIt: scripts/check-ldt-sha-comment-presence.mjs, run by the ci.yml job ldt-sha-comment-presence on every push to any branch and every pull_request.
P-329.whatTriggersIt: Every push and PR, unconditionally since this row removed the `if:`; the script itself is a no-op (PASS, not applicable) unless the diff's changes to cloudbuild.publish.yaml touch the _LDT_SHA value.
P-329.whatFails: Exit 1 with the report as JSON (the pin's value changed with no adjacent comment line); exit 2 with a reason when the base cannot be resolved at all (with either the declared base or the fallback ref), and for usage/setup errors.
P-329.whatBypassesIt: Committing the pin change and the comment in a way the diff does not show as an added line (e.g. amending an unreleased commit before it is ever pushed -- there is no diff to judge); editing the pin AND its comment instead of adding one (the check requires an ADDED comment line adjacent to the changed pin); `_LDT_SHA` being changed in a commit already reachable from the fallback ref; and the CI job being disabled or its step removed.

P-330.whatExecutesIt: src/jobs/county-runner.mjs (the county runner job/CLI verb) on each child failure: `declaredScopeRefusalFor` reads the child execution's task-attempt exit code through src/control/cloudrun-jobs.mjs and compares it against the plan's per-job declaration; src/cli.mjs exits with the declared code so the child's own exit status carries it.
P-330.whatTriggersIt: A child execution that did NOT succeed. Nothing is read for a job that declares no scope refusals (measured: zero reads), and nothing is read for a child that succeeded.
P-330.whatFails: A declared declaration that is malformed is refused by validatePlan (RUNNER_PLAN_INVALID) before a walk starts; the exit-code table refuses a duplicate or out-of-range entry (SCOPE_REFUSAL_EXIT_TABLE_INVALID); a walk stops with INSTRUMENT_FAILED naming the child and the reason when the code is undeclared, declared for another job, or unreadable.
P-330.whatBypassesIt: A child that exits with a declared code WITHOUT having declined the county (the code is a claim by the child; nothing verifies the child's reason, which is why the declaration names the file+constant that owns the scope and the band of codes is short); a child that declines and exits 0; a new county-scoped job that refuses a scope code and is not declared (it stops the walk -- safe, but the absence is unrecorded rather than declared); a job whose refusal is a store-less 60-79 exit for a reason that is not scope at all (the table is the only thing keeping those apart).

scopeAndLimits.notDone: No store write, no store read, no job execution against any target, no deploy, no schedule, no merge, no force-push, no rebase, no sub-agent (FAN-DEPTH 0). The only non-repo acts are read-only `gcloud run jobs describe` / `gcloud builds describe` / `gcloud artifacts docker tags list` calls against hauska-prod-497015, used to answer the P-334 rebuild question with measurements rather than assertion.
scopeAndLimits.customerSurface: None of the three rows is reachable from a customer surface: P-334 changes a factory watch job's resolver, P-329 changes a CI check, P-330 changes the county runner's control flow. Completion is a set of refusals/behaviours proven by violation in the repo's own suites and by the falsifier scripts, each re-derivable from the cited commands -- declared in the close as probe.notApplicable with its reason rather than filed as a probe artifact (the gate's own PREDICATE_DEBT path for OPS-24 rows with no surface predicate yet).
scopeAndLimits.ofScopeNotTouched: P-351 (the bake pin move) is untouched; ldt-pin-staleness is untouched; the P-321 band (0.90/0.50) and A-220's 0.05 threshold are untouched; factory-verify-walk's resolver-vs-mount mismatch is NAMED and asserted, not fixed (a different job's contract); P-256's IN_SCOPE_COUNTIES list is referenced, never copied.

openQuestionsForTheIntegrationSeat: P-334: a rebuild of cloudbuild.publish.yaml deploys the same digest to all seven jobs, so P-334 cannot ship alone -- it carries P-325 + P-327 + P-335 (see correctionsToDispatchPremise). Is that acceptable in one act, or does the seat want those three deployed and verified first?

P-330: the exit-code band (60-79) is a CLI contract. If another lane already reserves statuses in that range for something else, the table needs renumbering BEFORE any child depends on it; nothing else in src/cli.mjs exits 60-79 at 0f4558a (checked: 1 refusal, 2 usage, 3 and 4 a command's own verdict, 128+n signals).

P-330: should the declaration also cover future county-scoped jobs by default (stop-and-record) or stay opt-in per job? This row keeps it opt-in, which means a new refusal code silently stops a walk until someone declares it -- safe, but unrecorded.
